correctness.rationale: For all integers n≥2, B>0 and rung price t>0, strict logdet concavity on the full independent-edge feasible simplex gives a unique optimizer, and rotational invariance forces two common conductances. Fourier diagonalization and the Chebyshev root product give τ=n b^(2n−1)(T_n(1+a/b)+1). The derivative at zero equals [n²−(2n−1)t]/2, yielding the exact deletion threshold and unique positive interior optimizer. The hyperbolic Chebyshev derivative identity gives fixed-price and t_n/n→c limits by uniform sign bracketing and the unique positive limit root. The exact gain follows by substituting these limits in the finite tree polynomial. Rational cofactor checks and finite floating-point asymptotic examples support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The objective is the standard determinant/tree-connectivity criterion used for D-optimal estimation, and the design space permits every edge conductance independently. The theorem determines support exactly for all n and all relative prices, including deletion of an entire edge orbit at t=n²/(2n−1). The linear-in-size price crossover has a nontrivial hyperbolic limiting allocation and a provably greater-than-one determinant gain for 0<c<1/2. The fixed-price limit gives an explicit optimal spending fraction (one quarter at equal prices), distinct from equal-edge allocation. These facts are reusable design boundaries and not just computational curiosities.
